Enterprise Systems Architecture & Strategy: Own the architecture and roadmap for Lightium’s data platform, enterprise systems, and supporting infrastructure as we scale from pilot to volume.

Ensure that decisions across the data warehouse, PLM, ERP, MES, and HW/SW infrastructure reinforce one another rather than compete, and translate manufacturing and business needs into a coherent, pragmatic systems strategy that ensures data traceability across the company and across multiple locations and departments.

Build and maintain high level dashboards that allows both operations and leadership teams to track KPI. Be responsible for all the cloud computing and cloud storage solutions, including Azure, AWS, Google Computing (GC) to ensure a cost-effective and scalable operations for both simulations, data analysis and data storage.
Data & Analytics Platform: Own the database and data-warehouse architecture and the modeling of test and manufacturing data, scaling it to support higher production volumes. Design, build, and operate the databases, data pipelines, transformation and orchestration, and lakehouse behind it on a modern data stack.

Set the data contracts, naming conventions, and quality standards that keep data trustworthy and traceable as volume grows, and ensure the platform powers reliable analytics, BI, reporting, and internal tools at scale.
Data Security, Governance & Compliance: Own IT and data security and governance across the platform: access control (including external and internal Tier-based access), managing data encryption in transit and at rest, backups and disaster recovery, and clear ownership of who can access what.

Align the systems and data landscape with the relevant standards (ISO 9001 quality management and ISO/IEC 27001 information security) and design the access and data-segregation controls that ensures confidentiality, and support export-control compliance (ITAR, US EAR, and the Swiss Goods Control Act / dual-use regulations) when handling sensitive PIC technical data.
Enterprise Systems & Product Lifecycle: Own Aras Innovator (PLM) and the ERP (Oracle NetSuite) implementation, including ongoing rollout, configuration, and the integration between the two. Drive end-to-end product and document lifecycle traceability, from design through to manufacturing, measurements, reporting and shipment, and keep master data consistent and clean across systems.
MES Selection & Implementation: Scout the market for a Manufacturing Execution System (MES) platform that fits both R&D (with high flexibility) and production (with high scalability), and run the full supplier tender through to vendor selection. Lead the subsequent implementation and integration of the MES with PLM, ERP, and the data platform, so that process steps, run data, and traceability flow end-to-end as production scales.
Test Automation & Tool Integration: Own the automated wafer-scale test software built on OpenTAP, from architecture and build through production rollout. Define and maintain the data-exchange protocols between tools and systems, connecting PLM, ERP, test, MES, and the data warehouse, and partner with process and test engineering to keep automation reliable and scalable as production volume ramps.
Infrastructure, Vendors & Continuous Improvement: Own the reliability, security, and scaling of core infrastructure (Linux servers, virtualization, containerized services, object storage, and backups), from the lakehouse and storage layers to application hosting and manufacturing-adjacent systems, and manage projects, contracts, and SLAs with external IT vendors and managed-service providers.

Document architecture as living references, support the colleagues who use the systems day to day, and continuously improve how data and digital tools serve the company.
Technical Guidance & Mentorship: Act as the technical reference and architect for the wider engineering community, setting the direction, standards, and best practices that automation engineers, data and analytics engineers, DevOps engineers, and interns. Manage and mentor a small team of specialists, and guide them in their day-to-day work, and support the hiring process for these roles as the team grows around the architecture you define.

Educational Background: A degree in computer science, engineering, physics, or a related field, with a strong track record in enterprise or solutions architecture, ideally in a manufacturing or semiconductor environment. You have ideally designed and built enterprise systems architectures from scratch.
Technical Expertise: Hands-on experience with PLM (Aras Innovator or similar) and ERP systems, including their implementation and integration. A track record leading automated/robotic production or testing lines, preferably in a semiconductor industry or similar.

A strong database and data-engineering background (database and data-model design, data pipelines, transformation and orchestration, and data quality), hands-on with modern lakehouse and data platforms such as Databricks, Apache Iceberg, and Trino, and comfortable across both cloud and on-prem infrastructure, including containers, object storage, and lakehouse architectures.

A solid grasp of data security, encryption, backups, and access control. Vendor and contract management experience, including negotiating SLAs with managed-service providers. Familiarity with data-relevant standards (ISO 9001, ISO/IEC 27001) and export-control regimes (ITAR, US EAR, Swiss dual-use / Goods Control Act) is a strong asset.

Proficiency in modern AI solutions.
Mindset: Pragmatic and lean by instinct, happy to architect and to build with your own hands, and to solve problems through smart integration and vendor orchestration rather than headcount. The Department of Social Services (DSS) is comprised of the administrative units of the New York City Human Resources Administration (HRA) and the Department of Homeless Services (DHS).

HRA is dedicated to fighting poverty and income inequality by providing New Yorkers in need with essential benefits such as Food Assistance and Emergency Rental Assistance.

DHS is committed to preventing and addressing homelessness in New York City by employing a variety of innovative strategies to help families and individuals successfully exit shelter and return to self-sufficiency as quickly as possible.
Information Technology Services (ITS) is DSS’s technology services organization. ITS mission is to support the daily, emergent, and long-term needs of both agencies.

ITS creates and enhances the technology infrastructure and computer applications that support HRA and DHS and develops applications, including a variety of client eligibility and recertification systems, case management systems, housing systems, employment/work engagement services, revenue producing computer matches, claiming systems, and personnel systems.
Information Technology Services (ITS) is recruiting for one (1) Senior IT Architect, to function as Senior IT Solution Architect, who will:
· Develop, maintain, and present enterprise solution architecture artifacts, including system, business, data, security, integration, and technology architecture diagrams. Translate business requirements into target-state architecture, technical standards, design options, and implementation guidance for DSS systems and digital platforms.
· Lead architecture planning and technical direction for major DSS initiatives, including ACCESS HRA, Paperless Office Systems, Curam-related work, and new software products. Provide design, development, testing, deployment, documentation, training, and operational-readiness guidance across project teams.
· Conduct product evaluations, proofs of concept, and technical assessments for software products and platforms that support strategic business initiatives. Recommend solutions involving cloud computing frameworks such as SaaS, IaaS, and PaaS; web and mobile frameworks; multitier application frameworks; microservices; APIs; event-driven architecture; and predictive analytics.
· Prepare gap analyses, investment roadmaps, and future-state capability models for DSS technology ecosystems. Identify critical deficiencies in the ITS environment and recommend improvements to architecture governance, technology standards, decision rights, accountability, and enterprise design practices.
· Serve as technical lead or IT project manager for medium and large technology initiatives, including planning work activities, coordinating assigned resources, conducting status meetings, managing risks and issues, and communicating progress, decisions, and implementation status to stakeholders.
· Support application reliability and resiliency by ensuring regular health checks of major application components, including business continuity, disaster recovery, backup, recovery testing, data integrity, and cross-platform dependencies.
· Participate in senior leadership meetings and act as the technical reference for Curam-related design, development, testing, and deployment knowledge while providing technical input to estimate the functional scope.

1. A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college in computer science, information systems, engineering, mathematics or related field and six years of satisfactory full-time experience related to enterprise architecture, solutions architecture, network architecture and/or IT infrastructure systems; or

Maintain the practice’s reference architectures, reusable patterns, and technical accelerators.

Architect SAP Business AI solutions using AI Core, AI Launchpad, generative AI hub, grounding, retrieval, and Joule extensibility.

Resolve technical escalations during build, testing, cutover, and stabilization.

Chair architecture governance and arbitrate decisions where a local need conflicts with the coherence of the broader estate.

s.t:
Our NielsenIQ Technology teams are building and evolving Connect, a unified, global, open data ecosystem powered by AI, cloud and on-premises technologies. Clients around the world rely on NielsenIQ data and insights to innovate and grow.

As a Principal Architect within the Enterprise Architecture team, you will define architecture for key components and capabilities across NIQ platforms, ensuring alignment with business strategy, product objectives, technology standards, and the long-term platform vision.

You will partner with architecture peers, Product and Operations leaders, engineering leaders, and development teams to take solutions from initial requirements through design, delivery, and production operation.

A key focus of this role is shaping the responsible adoption of Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, and agentic AI across the enterprise.

The successful candidate will combine broad enterprise architecture experience with practical knowledge of AI-enabled systems and will grow into an end-to-end platform architect as their knowledge of NIQ's platforms expands.
Role Mandate: Act as the strategic Enterprise Architecture partner and single point of architecture accountability for an assigned NIQ product portfolio. The role connects business and product strategy to target-state architecture, capability ownership, technology roadmaps, governed standards, and delivery feedback.

It is intentionally strategic while remaining close enough to Product, Engineering, Solution Architecture, and Architecture Practice teams to ensure that direction is actionable and produces measurable outcomes.

Own and maintain the portfolio target-state architecture and rolling three-year technology roadmap, aligned with business priorities, product strategy, engineering plans, and enterprise transformation goals.
Serve as the named strategic architecture partner and single point of EA accountability for the assigned portfolio, building trusted working relationships with Product, Engineering, Operations, Data Science, Security, and business leadership.
Create and maintain business-capability, domain, application, data, and platform maps that expose ownership, dependencies, duplication, maturity gaps, lifecycle risk, and opportunities for simplification or growth.
Translate strategic priorities into clear architecture outcomes, transition states, investment options, sequencing recommendations, and measurable decision criteria.
Guide platform-placement and build-versus-buy decisions, balancing enterprise reuse and standards with appropriate portfolio autonomy, speed, cost, resilience, and client commitments.
Define and contribute reusable reference architectures, patterns, guardrails, and decision trees, including patterns for AI, Generative AI, agentic AI, data, integration, cloud, security, and observability.
Drive adoption of approved architecture standards and bring standards, reference architectures, major exceptions, and cross-functional decisions through the lightweight EA governance process for ratification.
Own visibility of portfolio architecture risks, strategic exceptions, technical debt, capability gaps, and cross portfolio dependencies; ensure actions, owners, and escalation paths are clear.
Partner with the Solution Architecture pillar to triage architecturally significant demand, shape initiatives early, and ensure delivery-level learning feeds back into portfolio strategy, standards, and roadmaps.
Assess emerging technologies and market shifts, especially AI and agentic commerce, and convert relevant signals into adoption guidance, controlled experiments, investment recommendations, and roadmap implications.
Enable self-service architecture by creating high-quality, reusable content for NIQ architecture knowledge repositories and supporting AI-enabled access to standards, patterns, decisions, and portfolio views.
Establish and run an effective operating cadence, including strategic portfolio reviews, intake alignment with Solution Architecture, reference artifact alignment with the Architecture Practice, and architect-only sessions to drive capability and domain consistency.
Define outcome-oriented measures for the portfolio, such as roadmap adoption, reuse, simplification, risk reduction, decision cycle time, standards adoption, and value realized from technology investments.
Support M&A due diligence and integration planning by assessing capability fit, architecture compatibility, technology risk, redundancy, security considerations, and potential integration paths.
Mentor architects and engineering leaders, communicate complex decisions clearly, and influence across organizational boundaries without relying on direct authority.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
10+ years of progressive experience across software engineering, solution architecture, platform architecture, or enterprise architecture, including significant experience with enterprise-scale products and data platforms.
Demonstrated ability to define target-state architectures and multi-year technology roadmaps, and to connect them to business capabilities, product objectives, investment decisions, and executable transition plans.
Experience operating as a strategic advisor to senior Product, Engineering, Technology, Operations, or business leaders, with evidence of influencing decisions across multiple organizations and geographies.
Strong knowledge of capability-based planning, domain and platform mapping, application rationalization, technology lifecycle management, technical debt, and architecture risk management.
Experience creating and driving adoption of enterprise standards, reference architectures, reusable patterns, architecture decision records, and governance processes that are pragmatic and lightweight.
Strong understanding of modern cloud, data, integration, API, security, resilience, observability, and distributed system architecture, preferably in Microsoft Azure and hybrid environments.
Knowledge of AI, Generative AI, and agentic AI architectures, including model and tool integration, retrieval augmented generation, orchestration, context and memory, evaluation, guardrails, observability, human oversight, and Responsible AI controls.
Ability to assess emerging technologies and develop clear build-versus-buy, adoption, migration, and total-cost of-ownership recommendations.
Experience partnering with Solution Architecture and delivery teams on architecturally significant initiatives while preserving a strategic, portfolio-wide perspective.
Excellent written, visual, and verbal communication skills, including the ability to express complex architecture choices as concise options, trade-offs, decisions, roadmaps, and executive-level narratives.
Proven facilitation, stakeholder management, negotiation, and conflict-resolution skills, with the ability to establish accountability and progress in a matrixed organization.
Experience in data, analytics, measurement, consumer intelligence, retail, media, or other information intensive product environments.
